rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up across the board: SUB and IBR get the highest security/diversity weights since they are cheap, low-risk transformations well suited to this program's many small hot functions (testA/B/C, stepA, initarray), while BCF and FLA are raised moderately to add control-flow confusion but with mid-range runtime/size cost weights so the optimizer can temper their overhead on the benchmark's timing loops. SPLIT stays lower because the largest function is only 139 text bytes, so splitting yields little hiding value relative to added call-graph noise; ICALL and IGV are kept at solid mid-high weights to obscure the call graph and global variable layout across the five-file program. CorrectnessRisk weights remain low-to-moderate everywhere to preserve the clean round-1 result while still allowing the selector freedom on non-critical functions.
